proofs.proof_tex:
We construct the two laws and verify every asserted property.  Fix
\[
 m=6,\qquad \eta=\frac1{10},\qquad \kappa=\frac1{20},
\]
and define
\[
 f_0(x)=(1-\eta)\frac{e^{-\sqrt2|x|}}{\sqrt2}
       +\eta c_6(1+x^2)^{-6},
 \qquad c_6=\frac{256}{63\pi}.
\]
The beta integral shows that both summands integrate to one.  Direct evaluation of the gamma-integral representation of \((1+x^2)^{-6}\), followed by the Gaussian Fourier integral, gives the positive even characteristic function
\[
 \phi_0(t)=\frac{1-\eta}{1+t^2/2}+\eta e^{-|t|}P_5(|t|),
\]
where
\[
 P_5(z)=1+z+\frac{4z^2}{9}+\frac{z^3}{9}
       +\frac{z^4}{63}+\frac{z^5}{945}.
\]
In particular, \(\phi_0(t)>0\) for every real \(t\).

Choose an even \(C^\infty\) function \(\chi:\mathbb R\to[0,1]\) that is one on \([-1,1]\) and zero outside \([-2,2]\).  For \(M\ge1\), let
\[
 \delta=\kappa M^{-2},\qquad
 \phi_{1,M}(t)=\phi_0(t)\left[1+\chi(t/M)
 \{e^{-\delta t^2/2}-1\}\right].
\]
We first verify, rather than assume, that \(\phi_{1,M}\) is a characteristic function for all sufficiently large \(M\).  If \(\varphi_\delta\) is the centered Gaussian density of variance \(\delta\), Fourier inversion gives the candidate density
\[
 f_{1,M}=f_0*\varphi_\delta+h_M,
 \qquad
 \widehat h_M(t)=\phi_0(t)\{1-\chi(t/M)\}
                    \{1-e^{-\delta t^2/2}\}.
\]
Put
\[
 b_M(z)=M^2\phi_0(Mz)\{1-\chi(z)\}
                    \{1-e^{-\kappa z^2/2}\}.
\]
For each integer \(0\le j\le12\), there is a finite \(B_j\), independent of \(M\), such that
\[
 \|b_M^{(j)}\|_1\le B_j. 
\]
Here is the uniform derivative check.  The factor \(1-\chi\) vanishes on \(|z|\le1\).  On \(|z|\ge1\), for each \(\ell\le12\),
\[
 \left|\partial_z^\ell\frac{M^2}{1+M^2z^2/2}\right|
 =\left|\partial_z^\ell\frac{2}{z^2+2M^{-2}}\right|
 \le C_\ell |z|^{-2-\ell}.
\]
Every derivative of the Student term is a finite sum bounded by terms of the form
\[
 M^{2+\ell+r}|z|^r e^{-M|z|}
 =|z|^{-2-\ell}(M|z|)^{2+\ell+r}e^{-M|z|},
\]
with \(r\) in a fixed finite range.  Since \(\sup_{y\ge1}y^a e^{-y}<\infty\) for fixed \(a\), these terms have integrable bounds independent of \(M\).  Derivatives of \(\chi\) are supported on \(1\le|z|\le2\), and derivatives of \(1-e^{-\kappa z^2/2}\) are bounded by a polynomial times a Gaussian.  The product rule therefore proves the displayed \(L^1\) bounds with constants fixed before \(M\) varies.

Under the stated Fourier convention,
\[
 h_M(x)=\frac1{2\pi M}\int_{\mathbb R}e^{-iMxz}b_M(z)\,dz.
\]
The bounds for \(j=0\) and twelve integrations by parts using the bound for \(j=12\) give a fixed \(A_{12}<\infty\) such that
\[
 |h_M(x)|\le A_{12}M^{-1}(1+M|x|)^{-12}.
\]
For \(\delta\le1\), retaining the Student component of \(f_0\) and restricting the Gaussian convolution to \(|z|\le1\) yields
\[
 (f_0*\varphi_\delta)(x)
 \ge \eta c_6 3^{-6}(1+x^2)^{-6}
      \Pr\{|N(0,\delta)|\le1\}
 \ge a_6(1+x^2)^{-6},
 \qquad a_6=\eta c_6 3^{-7}>0.
\]
We used \(1+(x-z)^2\le3(1+x^2)\) for \(|z|\le1\) and \(\Pr\{|N(0,\delta)|\le1\}\ge1/3\).  Since \((1+x^2)^6\le(1+M|x|)^{12}\),
\[
 \frac{|h_M(x)|}{(f_0*\varphi_\delta)(x)}
 \le\frac{A_{12}}{a_6M}.
\]
Thus \(f_{1,M}\ge0\) once \(M\ge2A_{12}/a_6\).  Also \(\widehat h_M(0)=0\), so \(f_{1,M}\) integrates to one.  It is even and therefore centered.  This establishes global positivity without treating the splice multiplier itself as a characteristic function; the compensation architecture is the one used for scalar fixed-envelope lower pairs by \cite{Meister2006}.

The spatial bound makes \(|x|^8|h_M(x)|\) integrable, while \(\widehat h_M\) vanishes on a neighborhood of zero.  Differentiation of the Fourier transform at zero consequently gives
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}x^j h_M(x)\,dx=0,
 \qquad 0\le j\le8.
\]
For a random variable \(S_6\) with density \(c_6(1+x^2)^{-6}\), another beta-integral calculation gives
\[
 \mathbb E S_6^{2j}
 =\frac{\Gamma(j+1/2)\Gamma(11/2-j)}
        {\sqrt\pi\,\Gamma(11/2)},
 \qquad 0\le j\le5.
\]
Combining this formula with the standardized-Laplace moments \((2j)!/2^j\), the even moments \(\mu_{2j}\) of \(f_0\) through order eight are
\[
 \mu_2=\frac{41}{45},\qquad
 \mu_4=\frac{227}{42},\qquad
 \mu_6=\frac{17011}{210},\qquad
 \mu_8=\frac{204121}{90}.
\]
If \(H_{1,M}\) has density \(f_{1,M}\) and \(H_0\) has density \(f_0\), the zero-moment identities show that the first eight moments of \(H_{1,M}\) equal those of \(H_0+N(0,\delta)\).  Hence, for \(0\le\delta\le1\),
\[
 \mathbb E H_{1,M}^8
 =\mu_8+28\delta\mu_6+210\delta^2\mu_4
  +420\delta^3\mu_2+105\delta^4
 \le\frac{554293}{90}.
\]

The splice multiplier is between \(e^{-2\kappa}\) and one: when \(\chi(t/M)\ne0\), \(|t|\le2M\) and \(e^{-\delta t^2/2}\ge e^{-2\kappa}\), while the multiplier is one off that support.  It follows from the positive rational term in \(\phi_0\) that both \(\phi_0\) and \(\phi_{1,M}\) are bounded above and below by positive constant multiples of \(|t|^{-2}\) for all sufficiently large \(|t|\).  If either source had a Gaussian divisor of variance \(r>0\), the residual characteristic function would have modulus
\[
 e^{rt^2/2}|\phi(t)|,
\]
which diverges as \(|t|\to\infty\), contradicting the modulus bound one for a characteristic function.  Both scalar sources are therefore Gaussian-indecomposable.

We now verify the experiment comparison, including the uniform derivative and weighted-Parseval steps.  Fix \(v=1/10\) and define
\[
 q_{0,M}=f_0*\varphi_{v+\delta},\qquad
 q_{1,M}=f_{1,M}*\varphi_v,
\]
with difference \(D_M=q_{0,M}-q_{1,M}\).  Its Fourier transform, up to the immaterial sign corresponding to this ordering, is
\[
 \widehat D_M(t)=e^{-vt^2/2}\phi_0(t)
 \{1-\chi(t/M)\}\{1-e^{-\delta t^2/2}\},
\]
and vanishes on \([-M,M]\).  Retaining the Student component and restricting a Gaussian convolution variable to a fixed compact interval gives a constant \(a_v>0\), uniform over \(0\le\delta\le\kappa\), such that
\[
 q_{0,M}(x)\ge a_v(1+x^2)^{-6}.
\]
Because \(f_0\) has finite sixth moment,
\[
 \sup_t|\phi_0^{(\ell)}(t)|\le\mathbb E|H_0|^\ell<\infty,
 \qquad 0\le\ell\le6.
\]
Derivatives of \(\chi(t/M)\) contribute bounded factors \(M^{-r}\), and derivatives of \(1-e^{-\delta t^2/2}\), with \(\delta=\kappa M^{-2}\), are uniformly bounded for \(M\ge1\).  Derivatives of the Gaussian factor are polynomials of degree at most the derivative order times the same Gaussian.  The product rule therefore yields, for \(0\le j\le6\), constants \(C_j\) independent of \(M\) such that
\[
 |\widehat D_M^{(j)}(t)|
 \le C_j(1+|t|)^j e^{-vt^2/2}
       \mathbf 1\{|t|\ge M\}.
\]
This bound puts every displayed derivative in \(L^2(\mathbb R)\).  Fourier differentiation in \(L^2\), followed by \(\mathrm{lem:parseval\text{-}identity}\), gives
\[
 \|x^jD_M\|_2^2=\frac1{2\pi}\|\widehat D_M^{(j)}\|_2^2,
 \qquad 0\le j\le6.
\]
Expanding \((1+x^2)^6\) now proves the exact weighted identity
\[
 \int_{\mathbb R}(1+x^2)^6|D_M(x)|^2\,dx
 =\frac1{2\pi}\sum_{j=0}^6\binom6j
   \|\widehat D_M^{(j)}\|_2^2.
\]
For \(M\ge1\), one integration by parts in each Gaussian tail, after extracting the largest polynomial power, implies
\[
 \int_{|t|\ge M}(1+|t|)^{2j}e^{-vt^2}\,dt
 \le C'_j(1+M)^{12}e^{-vM^2},
 \qquad 0\le j\le6.
\]
The lower density bound and the weighted identity therefore give a fixed \(A<\infty\) with
\[
 \chi^2(q_{1,M},q_{0,M})
 =\int\frac{|D_M(x)|^2}{q_{0,M}(x)}\,dx
 \le A(1+M)^{12}e^{-vM^2}.
\]
Independence and Fubini yield
\[
 1+\chi^2(q_{1,M}^{\otimes N},q_{0,M}^{\otimes N})
 =\{1+\chi^2(q_{1,M},q_{0,M})\}^N.
\]
Take \(M^2=30\log N\).  Since \(vM^2=3\log N\),
\[
 N\chi^2(q_{1,M},q_{0,M})
 \le A N^{-2}(1+\sqrt{30\log N})^{12}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Thus the product chi-square divergence tends to zero.  Cauchy--Schwarz applied to the likelihood-ratio difference gives
\[
 \|q_{1,M}^{\otimes N}-q_{0,M}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
 \le\frac12\sqrt{\chi^2(q_{1,M}^{\otimes N},q_{0,M}^{\otimes N})}
 \longrightarrow0.
\]

We embed this scalar pair into the three-dimensional model.  Let \(a=(1,2/5,1)^\top\), let \(\Gamma_\star\) be the displayed matrix, and put
\[
 \overline\Gamma=\Gamma_\star-vaa^\top.
\]
Its leading principal minors are \(9/10\), \(189/250\), and \(294/625\), so Sylvester's criterion gives \(\overline\Gamma\succ0\).  Apply to both scalar experiments the same Markov kernel \(z\mapsto az+G_{\overline\Gamma}\).  Total variation contracts under a Markov kernel; equivalently, conditional expectation of the likelihood ratio and Jensen's inequality contract chi-square divergence.  The kernel image of \(q_{1,M}\) is the first law below and that of \(q_{0,M}\) is the second:
\[
 P_{0,N}=\mathcal L(aH_{1,M}+G_{\Gamma_\star}),\qquad
 P_{1,N}=\mathcal L(aH_0+G_{\Gamma_\star+\delta aa^\top}).
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \|P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}-P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\longrightarrow0.
\]
Our choice of \(M\) gives
\[
 s_N=\delta=\frac{\kappa}{M^2}=\frac1{600\log N}.
\]

It remains to check the fixed class constants.  The leading principal minors of \(\Gamma_\star-I/10\) are
\[
 \frac9{10},\qquad \frac{13}{20},\qquad \frac{8109}{25000},
\]
and those of \(4I-\Gamma(1)\) are
\[
 2,\qquad \frac{126}{25},\qquad \frac{44}{125}.
\]
Since \(\Gamma(s)\) is increasing in Loewner order, Sylvester's criterion at the two endpoints yields
\[
 \frac1{10}I\prec\Gamma(s)\prec4I,
 \qquad 0\le s\le1.
\]

For every coordinate or pair-sum ray \(u\),
\[
 |a^\top u|\in\left\{\frac25,1,\frac75,2\right\}.
\]
Writing \(r=|a^\top u|\), direct algebra gives, for \(t\ge1\),
\[
 \frac12\le\frac{(1+t)^2}{1+r^2t^2/2}\le\frac{27}{2}.
\]
The rational component and the splice multiplier therefore give the uniform lower envelope
\[
 (1+t)^2|\phi_U(tu)|
 \ge\frac9{10}\cdot\frac12\,e^{-2\kappa}
 =\frac9{20}e^{-1/10}>\frac25.
\]
For the upper envelope, if \((1+z)^2P_5(z)=\sum_k d_kz^k\), direct expansion gives
\[
 \sum_kd_k k!=\frac{4714}{63}.
\]
Using \(e^{-z}z^k\le k!\) for \(z\ge0\), together with \((1+t)^2\le(25/4)(1+rt)^2\) for \(r\ge2/5\), yields
\[
 (1+t)^2|\phi_U(tu)|
 \le\frac9{10}\frac{27}{2}
   +\frac1{10}\frac{25}{4}\frac{4714}{63}
 =\frac{37117}{630}<60.
\]
The splice multiplier never exceeds one, so this bound applies to both laws.  Thus every named ray has exponent two with the common constants \(2/5\) and \(60\).

For either scalar source \(H\) used above, the moment calculation gives \(\mathbb EH^8\le554293/90\).  If \(Z_3\sim N(0,I_3)\), then \(\mathbb E\|Z_3\|^8=3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot9\).  The eighth-power triangle inequality, \(\|a\|_2^2=54/25\), and \(\|\Gamma^{1/2}\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le2\) give
\[
 \mathbb E\|aH+G_\Gamma\|^8
 \le2^7\left\{\left(\frac{54}{25}\right)^4\frac{554293}{90}
       +4^4(3\cdot5\cdot7\cdot9)\right\}
 <50000000.
\]
Normalize each scalar source by its standard deviation and multiply its loading by the same standard deviation; this leaves \(U=aH\) and hence the observational law unchanged.  The normalized source has unit variance.  Since \(\operatorname{Var}(H)\le41/45+1=86/45\), its adjusted loading obeys
\[
 \|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2
 \le\frac{54}{25}\frac{86}{45}
 =\frac{516}{125}<9.
\]
It has rank one, its sole column is lexicographically sorted, and its first nonzero entry is positive.

For an arbitrary direction \(u\in\mathbb R^3\), the source characteristic function along that direction is \(\phi_H(ta^\top u)\).  If \(a^\top u\ne0\), its logarithm grows only logarithmically by the polynomial tail; if \(a^\top u=0\), it is identically one.  Hence, for either constructed law,
\[
 -2t^{-2}\log|\phi_X(tu)|\longrightarrow u^\top\Gamma u.
\]
If \(\Delta\) were the covariance of any Gaussian convolution divisor of the same law, the residual characteristic function would have modulus at most one, so
\[
 e^{t^2u^\top\Delta u/2}|\phi_X(tu)|\le1.
\]
Taking logarithms, dividing by \(t^2/2\), and passing to the limit gives \(u^\top\Delta u\le u^\top\Gamma u\) for every \(u\).  Thus \(\Delta\preceq\Gamma\).  Since the displayed \(\Gamma\) is itself a divisor in the construction, it is the greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance.

Finally, along \(\Gamma(s)=\Gamma_\star+saa^\top\), direct substitution gives
\[
 \Gamma_{WY}(s)-\frac{\Gamma_{WT}(s)\Gamma_{TY}(s)}{\Gamma_{TT}(s)}=0,
 \qquad
 \frac{\Gamma_{TY}(s)}{\Gamma_{TT}(s)}
 =\frac{3/5+s}{1+s}=b(s).
\]
Under the partial order whose only relation is \(T\prec Y\), the treatment-predecessor ideals are \(\varnothing\) and \(\{W\}\).  The edge-collision identity in \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) therefore gives
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(s),\preceq)=\{b(s)\},
 \qquad 0\le s\le1.
\]
All spectral, envelope, loading, moment, greatest-divisor, and collision conditions have now been checked, so \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\subseteq\mathcal M_\star\).  By \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}class\text{-}sr\text{-}inclusion}\), these same \(k=1\) witnesses also lie in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\): independence is vacuous for one source, unit-variance normalization was explicit, rank is one, lexicographic ordering is vacuous, nonconstancy follows from positive variance, and Gaussian indecomposability implies both non-Gaussianity and absence of a Gaussian component.  This proves all assertions, including the published-class membership required for the lower-bound transfer.

added_lemmas.statement:
The fixed exponent-two class is contained in the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi observational class:
\[
 \mathcal M_\star\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}.
\]
added_lemmas.proof_tex: Take \(P_X\in\mathcal M_\star\).  By \(\mathrm{def:lower\text{-}class}\), \(P_X\in\mathcal M\), and \(\mathrm{def:fourier\text{-}model}\) supplies \(X=AH+G_\Gamma\) with \(H\perp G_\Gamma\), \(1\le k\le p\), mutually independent nonconstant source coordinates, \(\operatorname{Var}(H_j)=1\), \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=k\), lexicographically sorted columns, and no nondegenerate Gaussian convolution divisor for any \(H_j\).  Independence and the unit variances give \(\operatorname{Cov}(H)=I_k\).  A nonconstant Gaussian variable has a nondegenerate Gaussian convolution divisor (split its positive variance into two positive summands), so Gaussian indecomposability also implies that every \(H_j\) is non-Gaussian.  Every defining condition of \(\mathrm{def:sr\text{-}published\text{-}class}\) follows, proving \(P_X\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\).

added_lemmas.statement:
Let \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\) and \(s_N\) be the splice witnesses.  For each \(\mathcal A\in\{\mathcal M_\star,\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\}\), equip \(\mathcal A\) with covariance and compatible-effect target maps that agree with \(\Gamma(P)\) and \(\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\) on \(\mathcal M_\star\); their values off \(\mathcal M_\star\) are unrestricted.  Then
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\Gamma_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal A}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =\Omega((\log N)^{-1})
\]
and
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\Theta_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}}
 \sup_{P\in\mathcal A}
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}
 d_H\!\left(\widetilde\Theta_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)
 =\Omega((\log N)^{-1}).
\]
If a Borel compact-valued sequence \((S_N)\) is uniformly honest over \(\mathcal A\), meaning
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\inf_{P\in\mathcal A}P^{\otimes N}
 \{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq S_N\}\ge1-\alpha,
\]
then
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}
 \{\operatorname{diam}(S_N)\ge |b(s_N)-b(0)|\}\ge1-2\alpha,
 \qquad |b(s_N)-b(0)|\asymp(\log N)^{-1}.
\]
The same three lower conclusions hold for every statistical superclass containing \(\mathcal M_\star\), provided its covariance and compatible-effect target maps agree with \(\Gamma(P)\) and \(\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\) on \(\mathcal M_\star\).  No upper rate over \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\) is asserted.
added_lemmas.proof_tex:
By \(\mathrm{thm:smooth\text{-}splice\text{-}pair}\), for all sufficiently large \(N\), both witnesses lie in \(\mathcal M_\star\), their product-law total variation
\[
 \tau_N:=\|P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}-P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}
\]
tends to zero, and their covariance and effect targets are
\[
 \Gamma_{0,N}=\Gamma(0),\quad \Gamma_{1,N}=\Gamma(s_N),\qquad
 \mathcal T_{0,N}=\{b(0)\},\quad \mathcal T_{1,N}=\{b(s_N)\}.
\]
The inclusion \(\mathcal M_\star\subseteq\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\) follows from \(\mathrm{prop:lower\text{-}class\text{-}sr\text{-}inclusion}\).  Hence the witnesses lie in either displayed class and in every superclass described in the statement.

Since \(\Gamma(s)=\Gamma_\star+saa^\top\) and \(\|aa^\top\|_{\mathrm{op}}=\|a\|_2^2=54/25\), their covariance separation is
\[
 \delta_{\Gamma,N}:=\|\Gamma_{1,N}-\Gamma_{0,N}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 =\frac{54}{25}s_N.
\]
For an arbitrary measurable covariance estimator, define
\[
 E_N=\left\{\|\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{0,N}\|_{\mathrm{op}}<\frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}2\right\}.
\]
On \(E_N^c\), its loss under the first law is at least \(\delta_{\Gamma,N}/2\); on \(E_N\), the triangle inequality makes its loss under the second law greater than \(\delta_{\Gamma,N}/2\).  The event characterization of total variation gives
\[
 P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}(E_N)\ge P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}(E_N)-\tau_N.
\]
Consequently,
\[
 \mathbb E_{P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}}\|\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{0,N}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 +\mathbb E_{P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}}\|\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma_{1,N}\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \ge \frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}2(1-\tau_N).
\]
The larger of the two risks is at least half their sum, and therefore every class containing the witnesses satisfies
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\Gamma_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}}\sup_P
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}
 \ge \frac{\delta_{\Gamma,N}}4(1-\tau_N)
 =\frac{27}{50}s_N(1-\tau_N).
\]
Because \(s_N=(600\log N)^{-1}\) and \(\tau_N\to0\), this is the asserted logarithmic covariance lower bound.

For the effect target, the singleton identities yield the genuine target separation
\[
 \delta_{\Theta,N}:=d_H(\mathcal T_{0,N},\mathcal T_{1,N})
 =|b(s_N)-b(0)|
 =\frac{(2/5)s_N}{1+s_N}.
\]
For \(0<s_N\le1\),
\[
 \frac{s_N}{5}\le\delta_{\Theta,N}\le\frac{2s_N}{5}.
\]
Applying the preceding event argument in the metric space \((\mathcal K(\mathbb R),d_H)\), with the ball of radius \(\delta_{\Theta,N}/2\) around \(\mathcal T_{0,N}\), gives
\[
 \inf_{\widetilde\Theta_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}}\sup_P
 \mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}d_H\!\left(\widetilde\Theta_N,
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\right)
 \ge\frac{\delta_{\Theta,N}}4(1-\tau_N)
 =\Omega((\log N)^{-1}).
\]
This proves both minimax lower bounds without equating covariance loss to causal-target loss.

Finally, let \((S_N)\) satisfy the displayed uniform-honesty condition over any class containing the witnesses, and put
\[
 h_N=\inf_P P^{\otimes N}\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq)\subseteq S_N\}.
\]
Set
\[
 r_N=\left[(1-\alpha)-\inf_{m\ge N}h_m\right]_++N^{-1}.
\]
Then \(r_N\to0\) and \(h_N\ge1-\alpha-r_N\).  With
\[
 F_{0,N}=\{b(0)\in S_N\},\qquad F_{1,N}=\{b(s_N)\in S_N\},
\]
honesty at the two singleton targets gives
\[
 P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}(F_{0,N})\ge1-\alpha-r_N,qquad
 P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}(F_{1,N})\ge1-\alpha-r_N.
\]
The membership events are measurable because \(\{K:x\in K\}=\{K:d_H(K,K\cup\{x\})=0\}\) is closed in the Hausdorff hyperspace.  Total-variation transfer of the second event and the union bound give
\[
 P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}(F_{0,N}\cap F_{1,N})
 \ge1-2\alpha-2r_N-\tau_N.
\]
On this intersection, the definition of diameter yields
\[
 \operatorname{diam}(S_N)\ge|b(s_N)-b(0)|.
\]
Taking the lower limit proves the honest-diameter assertion.  The calculation of \(\delta_{\Theta,N}\) supplies its logarithmic order and uses exact singleton collisions, not a swap margin.

proposed.name: SRClass
proposed.def: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\) is the observational mixed-noise class satisfying Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi Assumptions 2--4.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The directive requires a typed symbol for the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi Assumptions 2--4 observational class so the splice inclusion and lower-bound transfer are formal core claims.

proposed.name: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi observational class
proposed.construction:
\(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\) is the class of centered observational laws \(P_X\) admitting a representation
\[
 X=AH+G_\Gamma,\qquad H\perp G_\Gamma,
\]
with \(1\le k\le p\), mutually independent coordinates \(H_1,\ldots,H_k\), \(\operatorname{Cov}(H)=I_k\), every \(H_j\) nonconstant and non-Gaussian and having no nondegenerate Gaussian convolution component, \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=k\), and the columns of \(A\) in ascending lexicographic order.  These are the observational restrictions in Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi Assumptions 2--4; no uniform Fourier envelope, spectral compactness, loading bound, or eighth-moment bound is included in \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{SR}}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: This records exactly the published structural restrictions named by the directive and deliberately excludes the extra Fourier, compactness, loading, and moment restrictions used for the upper rate.

proposed.statement:
For every sufficiently large \(N\), there are Borel laws \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\subseteq\mathcal M_\star\) and \(s_N=1/(600\log N)\) such that \(\Gamma(P_{0,N})=\Gamma(0)\), \(\Gamma(P_{1,N})=\Gamma(s_N)\), and \(\|P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}-P_{1,N}^{\otimes N}\|_{\mathrm{TV}}\to0\).  Both laws have a one-dimensional, unit-variance, Gaussian-indecomposable source representation with \(\operatorname{rank}(A)=1\) and \(\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}<A_{\max}=3\), obey \(q_u=2\) on every \(u\in\mathcal R\) with common lower envelope constant \(2/5\) and upper envelope constant \(60\), satisfy \(\mathbb E\|X\|^8\le M_8=50000000\), and have the displayed covariance as their greatest Gaussian-divisor covariance.  Moreover,
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P_{0,N}),\preceq)=\{b(0)\},\qquad
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P_{1,N}),\preceq)=\{b(s_N)\}.
\]

proposed_core_edits.reason: The proof now derives published-class membership through the new fixed-class inclusion proposition, so that load-bearing dependency must be recorded without changing the current claim text.

proposed.statement: The explicit construction in \(\mathrm{thm:smooth\text{-}splice\text{-}pair}\) yields \(\inf_{\widetilde\Gamma_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Gamma,N}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}\|\widetilde\Gamma_N-\Gamma(P)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\) and \(\inf_{\widetilde\Theta_N\in\mathfrak E_{\Theta,N}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_\star}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes N}}d_H(\widetilde\Theta_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma(P),\preceq))\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\). Moreover, for every \((S_N)\in\mathfrak C_\alpha(\mathcal M_\star)\), the constructed collision laws satisfy \(\liminf_{N\to\infty}P_{0,N}^{\otimes N}\{\operatorname{diam}(S_N)\ge|b(s_N)-b(0)|\}\ge1-2\alpha\), where \(P_{0,N},P_{1,N}\in\mathcal M_{\mathrm{col}}\) and \(|b(s_N)-b(0)|\asymp(\log N)^{-1}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The new two-point transfer theorem is now the declared source of the fixed-class lower halves and the published-class and superclass lower-only extensions; the matching upper halves still come solely from the fixed Fourier class.

prose_updates.tldr: Under mutually independent, unit-variance, nonconstant Gaussian-indecomposable latent sources, a full-column-rank identified loading convention, and an explicit greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition, a known partial order leaves a finite Cholesky-effect fiber. The note represents that fiber by treatment-predecessor ideals and maps a measurable finite-sample characteristic-function covariance region into simultaneous coverage of every compatible effect, including exact collisions. Expected covariance and Hausdorff errors are of order \(1/\log N\) on the fixed ordinary-smooth Fourier class. An explicit positive smooth Laplace--Student splice attains matching covariance, singleton-effect, and honest-diameter lower bounds there; because this fixed class is contained in the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi Assumptions 2--4 class, the three lower bounds also transfer to that published class and to every superclass containing the fixed splice class. No logarithmic upper bound is claimed for the broader published class. Literal standardized-Laplace sources form a root-\(N\) fourth-cumulant boundary.

project_justification.gap: Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi give finite population identification for mixed-noise models under their Assumptions 2--4, while Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov treat Fourier covariance recovery and Wang--Kolar--Drton propagate order uncertainty to one effect in a causally sufficient additive-error setting. These results do not provide a finite-sample event covering every partial-order-compatible Cholesky effect after greatest-Gaussian-divisor recovery, nor the exact-collision confidence-diameter lower bound proved here.
project_justification.niche: The upper and lower questions require different scopes. Honest finite-sample regions and matching rates are established on a fixed-dimensional class with known ordinary-smooth ray envelopes and compact spectral, loading, and moment bounds; the explicit lower witnesses additionally satisfy the broader Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi published source hypotheses.
project_justification.fill: The note supplies the predecessor-ideal functional, an explicit centered ray region with polarization, spectral clipping, and bounded fallback, finite-sample simultaneous whole-fiber coverage, a verified smooth splice with vanishing product total variation, matching logarithmic upper and lower rates on the fixed Fourier class, and lower-only covariance, causal-fiber, and honest-diameter transfer to the published class and every superclass containing the fixed splice class.

prose_updates.related_work: Sanjaroonpouri and Ramazi are the population-identification anchor. Their Assumptions 2--4 use mutually independent nonconstant non-Gaussian sources with no Gaussian component, \(1\le k\le p\), unit covariance normalization, lexicographically ordered reduced-loading columns, and full column rank. The fixed exponent-two Fourier class used here satisfies those hypotheses, while adding known Fourier envelopes and compact spectral, loading, and moment restrictions for uniform inference. The explicit splice witnesses therefore transfer logarithmic lower bounds to the published class, but the extra restrictions are essential to the upper proof and no upper rate over the full published class is asserted. The greatest-Gaussian-divisor condition remains explicit in the Fourier model and is verified directly for the witnesses. Belomestny, Trabs, and Tsybakov supply the multivariate characteristic-function polarization precedent, and Meister supplies the scalar fixed-envelope centering and compensated lower-pair architecture; the present proof verifies the six-degree positivity, uniform derivatives, weighted Parseval bound, and causal collision embedding. Wang, Kolar, and Drton study recursive causally sufficient additive-error models and asymptotic coverage of one effect after order and adjustment-set inference; no blanket inclusion relation between their full model and the present one is used. Perkovi\'c, Kalisch, and Maathuis connect background knowledge to IDA effect multisets, while the CRAN \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) and Maathuis et al. yeast intervention-ranking workflow motivate reporting an honest compatible-effect set under an audited mixed-noise/Fourier model rather than a selected Gaussian-causal-sufficiency list. Miettinen, Taskinen, Nordhausen, and Oja provide the fourth-cumulant estimating-equation precedent for the literal-Laplace boundary.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The logarithmic upper guarantee is uniform only with fixed dimension and known ray exponents, Fourier envelopes, spectral bounds, loading bound, and eighth-moment bound. The lower splice uses a fixed three-variable exponent-two class and conservative numerical constants; its independently checked derivative and weighted-Parseval estimates establish the claimed product indistinguishability but do not provide adaptation to unknown smoothness or a matching upper theorem over the unrestricted Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem-level deliverables are the exact ideal representation, collision-stable Lipschitz transfer, measurable finite-sample covariance and whole-fiber regions, \(O((\log N)^{-1})\) expected error on the fixed Fourier class, the explicit positive smooth-splice pair, matching fixed-class minimax and honest-diameter results, lower-only transfer to the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi class and every superclass containing the fixed splice class, and the uniformly quantified literal-Laplace boundary. No blanket nonnestedness theorem is claimed. The broader published class receives no upper-rate claim because it does not impose the uniform Fourier envelopes or compact spectral, loading, and moment bounds used by the estimator analysis. The proposal also does not claim adaptation to unknown exponents, growing-dimension guarantees, polynomial-delay ideal enumeration, correct singleton selection, or minimax sharpness for every exponent profile. When the partial order is total, the ideal family has one treatment-predecessor set and the fiber reduces to the usual singleton regression effect.

statement_notes.justification: The verified positive smooth splice supplies logarithmic covariance and singleton causal-target separations with vanishing product total variation. It matches the fixed Fourier-class upper bounds and forces an honest confidence set to contain both collision effects with limiting probability at least \(1-2\alpha\).
statement_notes.gap: Belomestny--Trabs--Tsybakov provide a covariance minimax precedent. This theorem adds an explicit moment-compatible three-variable lower pair, a distinct Hausdorff lower bound for the singleton causal-effect target, and a quantified honest-diameter event on an exact collision stratum. The lower construction also lies in the Sanjaroonpouri--Ramazi published class, so the lower conclusions transfer there without asserting a corresponding upper rate.
statement_notes.consumer: For the \(\texttt{pcalg::ida}\) and yeast intervention-ranking workflow, the result rules out uniformly faster audited mixed-noise effect precision through order selection or collision testing; an honest procedure must retain the logarithmic-scale compatible-effect uncertainty.

proofs.proof_tex:
Fix \(P_X\in\mathcal M\), and for \(J\in\mathcal J\) put \(S_J=D\cup J\).  We first record two consequences of the spectral hypotheses that will be used on both branches of the construction.  Let \(H,H'\) be positive-definite matrices whose spectra are contained in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\), and write \(\delta=\lVert H-H'\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\).  If \(Y\in S_J\), then the definition of partial covariance gives
\[
 \gamma_{YT\mathbin{\cdot}S_J}(H)
 =H_{YT}-H_{YS_J}H_{S_JS_J}^{-1}H_{S_JT}=0,
\]
because \(H_{YS_J}H_{S_JS_J}^{-1}\) is the coordinate row selecting \(Y\) from \(S_J\).  The denominator \(\gamma_{TT\mathbin{\cdot}S_J}(H)\) is strictly positive because it is the Schur complement of the positive-definite principal block \(H_{S_JS_J}\).  Hence \(\beta_J(H)=0\), and the same argument applies to \(H'\).

Suppose instead that \(Y\notin S_J\), and set \(B_J=S_J\cup\{T\}\).  The restriction \(T\ne Y\) in \(\mathrm{ass:distinct\text{-}targets}\) then gives \(Y\notin B_J\).  Block Gaussian elimination, equivalently the Schur-complement identity applied to the partition \(B_J=S_J\cup\{T\}\), yields
\[
 \beta_J(H)=e_T^{\mathsf T}H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}H_{B_JY}.
\]
Every principal submatrix of \(H\) and \(H'\) has smallest eigenvalue at least \(\lambda\), by \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}lower}\), while \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}upper}\) gives \(\lVert H_{B_JY}\rVert_2\le\Lambda\) and \(\lVert H'_{B_JY}\rVert_2\le\Lambda\).  Consequently
\[
 |\beta_J(H)|
 \le \lVert H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert H_{B_JY}\rVert_2
 \le \frac{\Lambda}{\lambda}.
\]
Moreover, the inverse identity
\[
 H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}-(H'_{B_JB_J})^{-1}
 =H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}
   \bigl(H'_{B_JB_J}-H_{B_JB_J}\bigr)
   (H'_{B_JB_J})^{-1}
\]
and the fact that restriction to a submatrix cannot increase the operator norm imply
\[
\begin{aligned}
 |\beta_J(H)-\beta_J(H')|
 &\le \lVert H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert H_{B_JY}-H'_{B_JY}\rVert_2 \\
 &\quad+
       \lVert H_{B_JB_J}^{-1}-(H'_{B_JB_J})^{-1}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
       \lVert H'_{B_JY}\rVert_2 \\
 &\le \left(\lambda^{-1}+\Lambda\lambda^{-2}\right)\delta
 =L_\beta\delta .
\end{aligned}
\tag{1}
\]
The preceding zero calculation shows that (1) also holds when \(Y\in S_J\).  Thus, for every \(J\in\mathcal J\),
\[
 |\beta_J(H)|\le\frac{\Lambda}{\lambda},
 \qquad
 |\beta_J(H)-\beta_J(H')|
 \le L_\beta\lVert H-H'\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.
\tag{2}
\]
This indexed estimate is consistent with the setwise bound in \(\mathrm{lem:fiber\text{-}lipschitz}\), but (2) also preserves the ideal label needed by the intervals in \(C_N\).

Consider first the fallback branch of \(\mathrm{def:ray\text{-}region}\).  By \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}lower}\), \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}upper}\), and the first inequality in (2), every \(\beta_J(\Gamma)\) lies in \([ -\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]\).  The exact identifying representation \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) therefore gives
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)
 =\{\beta_J(\Gamma):J\in\mathcal J\}
 \subseteq[-\Lambda/\lambda,\Lambda/\lambda]
 =C_N
\]
with probability one on that branch.

Now suppose that the active-branch conditions \(t_N\ge1\) and \(m_N\ge2\varepsilon_N\) hold.  Let \(\mathcal E_N\) be the simultaneous event furnished by \(\mathrm{thm:fourier\text{-}region}\), on which all its ray inequalities hold and
\[
 \lVert\widehat\Gamma_N-\Gamma\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}
 \le 2\Delta_N.
\tag{3}
\]
The same theorem, using \(\mathrm{ass:iid}\), gives uniformly over \(P_X\in\mathcal M\)
\[
 P_X^N(\mathcal E_N)\ge1-\alpha_N.
\tag{4}
\]
Spectral clipping in \(\mathrm{def:ray\text{-}region}\) puts the spectrum of \(\widehat\Gamma_N\) in \([\lambda,\Lambda]\); membership of \(P_X\) in \(\mathcal M\) and \(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}lower}\)--\(\mathrm{ass:spectral\text{-}upper}\) do the same for \(\Gamma\).  Applying (2) to (3) therefore gives, simultaneously for every ideal \(J\),
\[
 |\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)-\beta_J(\Gamma)|
 \le 2L_\beta\Delta_N.
\tag{5}
\]
Each \(\beta_J(\Gamma)\) is in the interval centered at \(\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)\) in \(\mathrm{def:fiber\text{-}region}\) by (5), and it is in the fixed clipping interval by (2).  Hence \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\) implies on \(\mathcal E_N\) that
\[
 \Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N.
\tag{6}
\]
Since \(\alpha_N=\min\{\alpha,(N+1)^{-2}\}\le\alpha\), equations (4)--(6), together with the probability-one fallback inclusion, yield for every \(N\)
\[
 \inf_{P_X\in\mathcal M}
 P_X^N\!\left\{\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\subseteq C_N\right\}
 \ge1-\alpha_N\ge1-\alpha.
\]

It remains to prove the directed excess assertion.  On the active branch and on \(\mathcal E_N\), take any \(x\in C_N\).  By the finite-union definition of \(C_N\), there is some \(J\in\mathcal J\) such that
\[
 |x-\beta_J(\widehat\Gamma_N)|\le2L_\beta\Delta_N.
\]
Because \(\beta_J(\Gamma)\in\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\) by \(\mathrm{prop:ideal\text{-}fiber}\), (5) and the triangle inequality give
\[
 \inf_{\theta\in\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)}|x-\theta|
 \le |x-\beta_J(\Gamma)|
 \le4L_\beta\Delta_N.
\]
Taking the supremum over \(x\in C_N\) proves
\[
 \operatorname{ex}\!\left(C_N,\Theta_{TY}(\Gamma,\preceq)\right)
 \le4L_\beta\Delta_N.
\]
No step chooses a linear extension or divides by a separation between distinct effect values: positive denominators follow solely from the spectral lower bound, and repeated values of different ideal branches remain covered by the same simultaneous argument.  Finally, the empirical characteristic-function coordinates are measurable finite sums, the positive floor makes every logarithm measurable and finite, spectral clipping is continuous on symmetric matrices, and each \(\beta_J\) is continuous on the spectrally bounded positive-definite set.  Since \(\mathcal J\) is finite by \(\mathrm{ass:order}\) and finiteness of \(V\), \(C_N\) is a measurable nonempty compact random set on either branch, so all displayed coverage events are measurable.
